neighbours.label: the expected partner word that closes a pairing in a run of parallel statements (the wife … her 'husband'; spiders spin 'webs'; Parents … their 'children'; the Moon … the 'Earth'); parallel statements that end on an unrelated word stay quiet
fire: Bakers bake bread, brewers brew beer, and spiders spin webs.
Teachers worry about their pupils, and mothers worry about their children.
Just as birds are born to fly, fish are born to swim.
Sheepdogs love herding sheep, and cattle dogs love rounding up cattle.
The king turned to his queen, and the wife looked at her husband.
The Scarecrow wanted a brain, and the Tin Man wanted a heart.
A planet circles its star much as the Moon circles the Earth.
Doctors care for patients, and shepherds care for their sheep.
quiet: Bakers open early, brewers open late, and tourists arrive whenever.
Teachers worry about their pensions, and mothers worry about the weather.
Just as trains are built to last, laws are written to change.
Sheepdogs love the snow, and cattle dogs love the car.
The king turned to the window, and the wife looked at her watch.
The Scarecrow wanted a holiday, and the Tin Man wanted a nap.
A planet cools slowly much as the Moon lost its warmth.
Doctors complain about paperwork, and shepherds complain about the rain.

notes: Card and look: husband, children, Earth, swim, cattle, child, heart, webs, each the natural counterpart of an earlier word inside a series of parallel clauses. Probe of the pairing in single sentences was weak (groom 0.14, patient 0.17, fly 0.13, Earth 0.02), so the test adds the parallel series. Low confidence; expect a fail.
